subject: Dedicated capacity: proposal for priority steering + soft guarantee
messages:
From: Sri Patel <sri.patel@edgewave.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@edgewave.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: dedicated capacity handling + carveout language

Hi Vanessa / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to capture a few contract-level asks from our platform engineering team that we need addressed before the SOW signs:

- During scheduled maintenance and planned capacity rebalancing, we need a mechanism to ensure high-priority inference traffic can be steered to reserved GPUs (or warm standby) to avoid tail latency spikes.
- We also want a defined headroom/crediting model if preemption or queueing causes sustained tail-latency breaches during business hours (Mon-Fri 8am-6pm PT).
- Clarify the behavior when our jobs and lower-priority customers contend for shared pools (queueing semantics, fair-share, and preemption windows).

I attached a short spreadsheet with our expected traffic profile and peak windows (edgewave-sla-requirements.xlsx). Can Redwood propose a contract amendment (even a "soft guarantee" addendum) that documents steering behavior, an availability target for reserved GPUs during our business hours, and a crediting approach (not necessarily full SLA credits, but something predictable)?

Timeline: Procurement would like draft language by end of day Jul 5 so legal can start review. Is that realistic?

Thanks,
Sri
Sri Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeWave Systems

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sri Patel <sri.patel@edgewave.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated capacity handling + carveout language

Sri — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. We can put a concise addendum together that covers steering, a soft availability commitment during your business hours, and an explicit remedial crediting formula.

High level proposal (for discussion):
- Priority steering: Redwood will provide a configurable priority lane for EdgeWave’s tenant on their Dedicated pool. Requests tagged with EdgeWave priority will be routed to either reserved instances or a warm standby pool before being routed to shared capacity.
- Soft availability target: 99.5% availability for reserved GPUs during Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 PT across your committed nodes, measured as scheduled_polling-window uptime excluding force-maintenances. This will be a "soft guarantee" — i.e. breaches trigger predefined credits rather than termination rights.
- Crediting: On a per-incident basis, if the measured 95th-percentile tail latency for priority-tagged requests exceeds 2.5x the baseline for more than 30 continuous minutes, Redwood will issue a credit equal to 5% of that month’s Dedicated fee for each qualifying incident, up to a 30% monthly cap.
- Queueing & preemption behavior: lower-priority traffic will be respectfully backpressured; preemption windows will be bounded to no more than X minutes per 24-hour period (we'll fill the exact X in the draft). We can include a playbook describing observable signals and a notification cadence.

Attached is a first-pass addendum PDF (redwood-soft-guarantee-draft.pdf). It is deliberately concise so legal can iterate quickly. Ben — adding you for the queueing/backpressure language accuracy. Lauren — can you review credits / commercial framing?

If this looks directionally correct, I can schedule a 30-min call with your procurement/legal tomorrow afternoon and circulate an editable DOCX.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Sri Patel <sri.patel@edgewave.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@edgewave.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Jul 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated capacity handling + carveout language

Vanessa — this is helpful, thank you. A few clarifications from our SRE lead:

1) The 30-minute continuous-min threshold seems reasonable, but can you confirm how continuous is defined around short maintenance windows? For example, if there are two 20-minute blips separated by a 10-minute window, do they count as separate incidents?

2) The preemption cap expressed as "X minutes" needs to be concrete for procurement. Can we propose something like "preemption events related to cross-tenant rebalancing will not account for more than 60 minutes of cumulative preemption during business hours per calendar week"?

3) How will priority-tagging be implemented from our side? Do we need SDK changes or will HTTP header tags suffice?

Procurement also asked if Redwood can provide an operational runbook that maps observed metrics (queue depth, tail latency, KV cache miss rate) to expected remediation steps and credit triggers. That would speed review dramatically.

Sri

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sri Patel <sri.patel@edgewave.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Jul 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated capacity handling + carveout language

Sri — quick technical note to address the SRE questions above: 

- Incident continuity: we define a continuous incident window as any contiguous period where the 95th-percentile tail latency for priority-tagged requests exceeds the agreed threshold. Non-contiguous windows separated by more than 15 minutes are treated as separate incidents. So in your example (20m blip, 10m normal, 20m blip) that would be two incidents because of the 10-minute healthy gap. We can adjust the separation window to 10/20 minutes if you prefer.

- Preemption accounting: the proposed 60 minutes cumulative per calendar week during business hours is reasonable. We track preemption time per tenant and can include a weekly report in the runbook. Preemption here refers to active evictions or forced migration for capacity rebalancing; transient queuing before placement is not counted as preemption but is observable in queue depth metrics.

- Priority tagging: header-level priority tags are sufficient. We’ll provide an API flag and SDK helper for your integration teams; both will set an `X-Redwood-Priority: edgewave-high` header. Requests with that header are placed into the priority lane and will consume from your reserved tokens first.

- Runbook: we'll produce a short operational runbook mapping metric thresholds to remediation steps (e.g., increase reserved nodes, disable background warm-up jobs, temporarily throttle non-critical jobs) and the crediting triggers.

I’ll prepare a short technical appendix to the addendum that includes observability keys and example query snippets.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Sri — appreciate the quick back-and-forth. Next steps:

1) Ben will finalize the technical appendix and incident separation definition (we will use 15 minutes by default).
2) Lauren and I will tweak the commercial language to replace X with the concrete 60-minute weekly preemption cap and clarify the crediting formula.
3) I’ll send the editable DOCX to your procurement and legal via DocuSign by tomorrow morning and include the runbook appendix.

Can we lock a 30-minute legal/ops sync tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT? If that works, I’ll send the invite and include a brief agenda: draft addendum review, incident handling, crediting examples.

Thanks — Vanessa
